statements: Create breaks.mjs at the workspace root: an ES module with one named function export, breakLines(words, width). Use Node.js built-ins only and no dependencies. Tests, if you write any, go under test/.

Checks run in this order, the first failure decides: words is not an array, or an entry (taken in index order) is not a string, TypeError code 'E_TYPE'; width is not a number with an integer value (so NaN, Infinity and 2.5 fail), TypeError code 'E_TYPE'; width is less than 1, RangeError code 'E_WIDTH'; an entry is empty or contains a space character (U+0020), RangeError code 'E_WORD'.

The result is an array of lines, in order. A line is its words joined by single space characters; every word appears once, in the given order. No words gives an empty array. The length of a line is its string length (UTF-16 code units), so a character outside the basic plane counts 2.
A line of two or more words has length at most width. A line of exactly one word may be longer than width, whatever the word.

A line costs: when it is not the last line and fits, the square of (width minus its length); when it is a single word longer than width, 0, last line or not; when it is the last line and fits, 0, except 6 if it is not the only line and holds exactly one word.
The result is a break placement with the smallest total cost of its lines.

Among placements of equal total cost, the result is the one whose first line is the longest; if the first lines have equal length, the one whose second line is the longest, and so on to the first line where two placements differ in length.
The function is pure: no I/O, no shared state, and the input array is not mutated.
brief: Implement breaks.mjs exactly as the numbered statements specify, then stop. Do not change any other file except tests under test/.
